main_text.l: pars, de principiis disciplinarum, scilicet uni-

l.i: cimus non simpliciter, sed cum restrictione per duo ad-
verbia. Disciplinæ enim considerantur tribus modis:
vel universaliter, vel communiter, vel singulariter.
Universaliter, quatenus habent principia remota
communia. Communiter, quatenus habent principia
propinqua communia. Singulariter, quatenus quae-
libet disciplina propria agnoscit principia. Sic v.g. Ma-
thefis, Physica, Ethica & aliæ disciplinæ habent prin-
cipia universalia, quæ sunt Sensus, Ratio, Scriptura,
& similia. At Geographia & Astrologia habent prin-
cipia communia, physica scilicet; ita Logica & Gram-
matica habent communia principia κοινὰ[?], prae-
ter illa universalia. Logica deniq; sua sibi habet pri-
ncipia: sic & Grammatica. Archelogia autem munus
est, explicare principia disciplinarum universalia &
communia. Singularia explicat quaelibet disciplina
specie. Clarius dicam. Archelogiam consideremus-
veluti alphabetum. Alphabetum hoc est vel com-
mune omnibus disciplinis, vel proprium theoreticis,
practicis, poëticis, & sic deinceps. Aliud enim est
alphabetum theoreticum, aliud practicum, aliud poët-
icum. Ita aut omnino duæ futuræ sint partes hujus no-
stræ Archelogiæ, quam tali methodo conscribemus, ut
ea neq; nimis supina, neq; etiam superstitiosa futura
sit. Nam sicut τὸ λίαν ἀκριβὲς ψεῦδ[?]ς: ita & τὸ λίαν

page.notes: Two marginal notes on the left: "Disciplinæ tribus modis disconsiderantur." (set in three lines, hyphenated at line ends) and "Archelogia est communis, vel propria." Greek κοινὰ and the final Greek word ψεῦδος are partly unclear on the scan. The final Greek word is read as ψεῦδ[?]ς. Printed spelling kept, including "Mathefis", "deniq;" and "ꞩ" forms converted to plain s. The chapter heading "Cap.12.De nostrâ methodo." is printed as "Cap. 12.De nostrâ methodo." on one line and is given as one head. Scan shows a stray mark after "est" that is not text and is left out.
